evidence.observation: localExec spawns a shell command, buffers stdout/stderr, and on close() rejects with `new Error((stderr || stdout || `Command failed with exit code ${code}`).trim())` (line 129); on the child 'error' event it rejects the raw spawn error (line 135); on timeout it rejects `Command timed out after Ns` (line 144). Because the message is a single `||`-chosen string, the exit code is discarded whenever stderr is non-empty, stdout is discarded whenever stderr exists, and `signal`, `timedOut`, and the native error code are never represented on the rejection. A child kill path (SIGTERM then SIGKILL, lines 139-143) is likewise indistinguishable from a normal non-zero exit to the caller.

gatewayExec is the only exported command entry point used by server handlers (server/handlers/files.js, skill-store.js, workspace.js, backup.js); it is a thin delegation to localExec, so every handler inherits the same lossy Error rejection and must wrap calls in try/catch, forwarding only err.message (e.g. server/handlers/files.js 'File not found' at the target-realpath catch). This is the exact seam where the structured normalization belongs.

Establishes the repository's normalized server-result contract: the function never rejects — every HTTP, fallback, parse, or thrown error is converted to a structured envelope, returning `{ ok: true, payload }` on success (lines 96, 110) and `{ ok: false, error: <message> }` on failure (lines 100, 103, 114, 118). The terminal catch at line 115-118 maps an arbitrary thrown Error to `{ ok: false, error: err.message }` inside a `finally`-guarded function. This is the shape the command-failure normalizer mirrors so the diagnostics captured at the child-process layer survive to the server result.

Confirms the contract is applied consistently across the core Gateway surface, not just RPC: non-OK responses return `{ ok: false, error: `Gateway HTTP ${status}` }` (line 145) and the catch block returns `{ ok: false, error: err.message }` (line 154), again never throwing. Reinforces that a structured, never-throwing result envelope with a diagnostic `error` field is the expected server-result form in this repo.

The delivered operation: maps a raw child-process failure object into the gateway-client result envelope (`ok: false` plus a full `error` object with code, message, command, causeCode, exitCode, signal, stdout, stderr, timedOut, durationMs). Classification in `classify` distinguishes non-zero exit, spawn failure, and timeout while preserving the native OS cause code separately, so no diagnostic that localExec currently drops is lost.

claims.claim: server/core/system.js localExec collapses distinct child-process failure modes into a single opaque Error, losing exitCode, stdout, signal, and the timedOut flag; because gatewayExec delegates to localExec, every server handler that runs a command inherits this diagnostic loss.

server/core/gateway-client.js already defines the target normalization contract: gatewayAdminRpcForTarget and gatewayHttpGet never reject and instead return a structured `{ ok: true, payload }` / `{ ok: false, error }` server result, so the command-failure fix is to emit that same envelope rather than throw.

Normalizing command failures into the gateway-client envelope is compatible across both layers: gatewayExec's throw-based failure is caught and re-expressed as `{ ok: false, error: {...} }`, preserving exitCode, signal, stdout/stderr separation, timedOut, and the native cause code that the original Error message discards.

conclusion: The cross-repository pattern 'normalize failure into a structured result instead of throwing' transfers cleanly to WattClaw. The repo already proves the contract in server/core/gateway-client.js (structured `{ ok, error }`, never throwing), while server/core/system.js localExec delegates command execution through a lossy single-message Error. The delivered executable demo, scripts/normalize-command-failure.mjs, applies the gateway-client envelope to fake backend/child-process failures (non-zero exit, spawn ENOENT, timeout, plus a clean run), preserving every diagnostic localExec drops — exitCode, signal, separated stdout/stderr, timedOut, native causeCode, command, and durationMs — and passes all 13 self-check assertions with exit code 0. No production behavior, package locks, task metadata, or git configuration were modified; the only repository change is the new demo script plus the required .prale-eval artifacts.
